page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dlsv7 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes hyper-threading with 2 threads per core, 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The Intel Xeon processor delivers top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench (score of 2267.0) and strong text processing capabilities (score of 2567.0). However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are significantly constrained. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores are categorized as poor and weak respectively, reflecting the physical limitation of a single underlying core. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 22.83 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 11.59 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10% tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are similarly weak to poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ls_v7 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring high clock-speed single-threaded execution without the overhead of large memory allocations. The inclusion of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), provides hardware-accelerated execution for specific cryptographic and integer operations despite the low memory footprint. This server is suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, simple web serving, and low-demand utility workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or multi-core scaling.
